g.text: GRU alternative: one numeric encoder + consolidated retrieval
Generic architecture | Three GRU layers of 32 units | One 128-unit prediction head
A Encode the predictors available before response t
Recency; item age; prior mean spacing; spacing-availability flag
Student logitdec; student-item logitdec; student-item PPES
Input dropout 0.1 produces x(t), shared by retrieval, prediction and memory update
Connector labels count weights; receiving boxes list biases. I and S are learned category counts, not fixed dataset sizes.
B Filter and retrieve completed memories: one head, width 32
Past completed events from this participant
Newest 100 global events: e(j), post-answer h3(j), raw item/skill IDs
Keep same item OR same skill-combination ID; compare exact raw IDs (0 parameters)
Weighted mean: m(t) = Σ a(t,j) h3(j)
* Q/K is one shared map: 3,072 weights + 32 biases total.
No learned attention decay; no attention dropout.
C Predict the current response; the answer is still unknown
Retrieved memory replaces direct h3(t−1) input to the head. Prediction never uses the current answer.
D Observe the binary answer, update memory, then write the bank
Keep h1(t), h2(t), h3(t) for the next trial: 3 × 32 state values
Append [pre-answer e(t): 96, post-answer h3(t): 32, raw IDs] to the newest-100-event bank; 0 parameters
All weights learn jointly from response-prediction loss. The seven-input encoder replaces the separate time/history networks.
At a new participant: zero GRU states and an empty bank; retain trained embeddings. Retrieval feeds prediction only.
Timing uses log(1 + seconds); numeric scaling and vocabularies use training participants only. Missing spacing has an availability flag.
Only completed scored responses update memory. Dropout is off for evaluation; gradients detach at 100-event BPTT chunk boundaries.
Architecture widths are fixed for this alternative. Item and skill-combination table sizes depend on the training vocabulary.
